replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: To solve a second order algebraic equation, start by writing it in standard form. Then, determine if it can be factored easily. To find stationary points of y=f(x), first compute the derivative f '(x). Set f '(x)=0 and solve for x. These x-values are candidates for stationary points. Next, evaluate f(x) at these points to get the corresponding y-coordinates. Finally, use the second derivative test or analyze the sign changes of f '(x) to classify each point as a local maximum, minimum, or saddle point.
